context:
Patient: 59F, breast cancer survivor (2016: dose-dense AC, cumulative doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left breast RT, on anastrozole), presents with left axillary mass, fevers to 38.4 C, drenching night sweats; ECOG 1, LDH 510. Non-GCB DLBCL (MYC 45%, BCL2 70%, FISH negative for rearrangements), PET nodes above and below the diaphragm plus splenic nodules, marrow negative, and new LVEF 45% (62% in 2016) with GLS -14%.
What this case tests: Spleen is a nodal site under Lugano, so stage is III, not IV, and IPI is 2. | Double-expressor by IHC but FISH-negative, so not double-hit; no intensification to DA-EPOCH-R. | Prior doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left chest RT and LVEF 62% to 45% mean standard full-dose R-CHOP / Pola-R-CHP is not safe as is. | Treatment must stay curative: anthracycline-free (R-CEOP / R-GCVP) or cardio-protected regimen, with cardio-oncology input and cardioprotective drugs. | CNS-IPI 2 with no high-risk sites: no routine CNS prophylaxis.

answer.diagnosis: Newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, NOS, presenting as a left axillary nodal mass (excisional biopsy 2026-08-25). Non-germinal-center B-cell phenotype by Hans algorithm (CD10 neg, BCL6 pos, MUM1/IRF4 pos ~80%), CD20 pos, PAX5 pos, CD3/CD5/CD10/cyclin D1/CD30 neg, EBER neg, Ki-67 ~80%, kappa-restricted B-cell population by flow. Double-expressor phenotype (MYC IHC 45%, BCL2 IHC 70%). Interphase FISH negative for MYC, BCL2 and BCL6 rearrangements, so this is not double-hit or triple-hit lymphoma. Bone marrow not involved. This is a new lymphoma, not a breast cancer recurrence: AE1/AE3 and GATA3 are negative in the lesional cells, there is no carcinoma morphology, and the immunophenotype is lymphoid. Background: left breast IDC 2016 (pT2 pN0, stage IIA, ER+ PR+ HER2-), treated with surgery, AC then paclitaxel, breast RT and anastrozole since 2016-11; no evidence of breast disease on PET or mammogram 2026-03. Hypertension and osteopenia.
answer.stage: Ann Arbor stage III-B-S (Lugano stage III). Disease above and below the diaphragm: left axillary, mediastinal (prevascular and paratracheal), para-aortic and mesenteric nodes, plus multiple FDG-avid splenic nodules (spleen counted as a nodal/lymphoid site, so S modifier and not stage IV). B symptoms present: fevers to 38.4 C, 38.2 C on 2026-09-15, and drenching night sweats; weight loss is about 3.7% over 6 months, below the 10% criterion, so B status rests on fever plus sweats. No FDG-avid marrow, liver, lung or bone disease on PET or on the negative marrow biopsy. Bulk: largest mass is the 7.5 cm mesenteric conglomerate on PET, below the 10 cm Lugano bulky threshold but at the 7.5 cm threshold used in some protocols. Baseline PET lesions (SUVmax 15 to 22) are far above liver SUVmax 2.7, which is consistent with Deauville 4-5 at baseline. If the splenic nodules were judged extranodal the stage would be IV, which would change the IPI by one point; I do not think that reading applies here.
answer.biology: Non-GCB (ABC-like by Hans) double-expressor DLBCL with very high proliferation (Ki-67 ~80%). No MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement by FISH, so it does not meet the double-hit definition and does not by itself indicate DA-EPOCH-R. Double expression (MYC IHC >=40% with BCL2 IHC >=50%) is adverse, mainly in non-GCB disease, and it raises the value of effective front-line therapy and of CNS and relapse risk assessment. Recommend, but do not gate treatment on: targeted NGS for MYD88 L265P and CD79B (MCD vs ABC signature), TP53 mutation or deletion, and gene-expression cell-of-origin if available. Ask pathology to confirm MYC IHC on block A2 and to document whether MYC rearrangement was tested with a second method, because a MYC rearrangement found by karyotype or NGS would reclassify her as double-hit.
answer.prognosis: Classic IPI 2 (low-intermediate): age 59 (0), LDH elevated (1), stage III (1), ECOG 1 (0), extranodal sites 0 (1 if the spleen is counted, which would give IPI 3, intermediate). NCCN-IPI about 4 (high-intermediate): age 41-60 (1), stage III-IV (2), LDH above ULN (1). CNS-IPI 2 (intermediate). Adverse features on top of the scores: double-expressor phenotype, non-GCB, B symptoms, bulk, B2M 2.9 mg/L (high) and Ki-67 80%. Standard full-dose R-CHOP for this IPI group gives an expected long-term cure in roughly the two-thirds to three-quarters range; with double expression the figure is lower, and I expect her outcome to be somewhat worse than the trial benchmark because cardiac limits prevent full anthracycline exposure. I cannot quote a validated figure for the anthracycline-free regimen I recommend. Prognosis is guarded but treatable and curative intent is appropriate.
answer.first_line_treatment: Curative intent, R-CHOP-type therapy is not recommended for her now. No anthracycline-containing regimen (R-CHOP-21, pola-R-CHP or DA-EPOCH-R) should be given at this time. Her LVEF has fallen from 62% (2016) to 45% with GLS -14% after cumulative doxorubicin 240 mg/m2 and left breast RT. Six cycles of doxorubicin 50 mg/m2 would take her cumulative exposure to about 540 mg/m2, above the usual 400-550 mg/m2 lifetime range where heart failure risk rises, and she already has LVEF below 50%. My decision is an anthracycline-free regimen: polatuzumab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg, rituximab 375 mg/m2, cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2, vincristine 1.4 mg/m2 (max 2 mg), and prednisone 100 mg on days 1-5, every 21 days for 6 cycles (pola-R-CVP). Polatuzumab benefit is established only with doxorubicin-containing R-CHP, so this is off-label and its added benefit is unproven; if polatuzumab is not accessible, R-CVP alone is the guideline-listed anthracycline-free fallback, accepting a lower expected cure rate. Enrollment in an anthracycline-free or cardio-protected lymphoma trial is preferred if one is open within about 3 weeks. Timing: start within about 2-3 weeks, after cardio-oncology review and a few weeks of cardiac medical therapy; the disease is not an emergency (no airway, cord, renal or CNS compromise, normal creatinine, uric acid 5.8). Rituximab is continued through all cycles. I would not add doxorubicin back later as a default; reconsidering a capped, cardio-protected anthracycline course would need LVEF recovery to at least 50% with improved strain and explicit cardio-oncology sign-off. Dexrazoxane is an option only if anthracycline is ever reintroduced. Prednisone-based regimens raise BP and fluid load, so monitor weight and BP each cycle.
answer.cns_risk: CNS-IPI 2 (intermediate): LDH elevated (1) and stage III (1); age 59 (not >60), ECOG 1, and normal kidneys and adrenals score 0. No testicular, paranasal sinus, bone marrow, or DH/TH involvement. Routine CNS-directed prophylaxis (intrathecal methotrexate or high-dose methotrexate) is not indicated on current criteria; the methotrexate toxicity would add to her cardiac and treatment burden without a clear net benefit. Double-expressor phenotype is a soft adverse feature, so I would document it as intermediate risk and reassess if new high-risk features emerge. No baseline brain MRI or lumbar puncture is needed unless she develops neurological symptoms, visual change, cranial nerve signs, or confusion. A baseline ophthalmology exam is optional and at the team's discretion. Re-evaluate if pathology reclassifies her as double-hit, if a CNS-IPI component changes, or if relapse involves the CNS.
answer.response_assessment: Baseline: FDG-PET-CT 2026-09-04 (Deauville score not reported; radiology to add it, since lesion SUVmax 15-22 vs liver 2.7 is consistent with Deauville 4-5). Clinical baseline: B symptoms, LDH 510 U/L, 2 cm residual left axillary node, palpable spleen tip, ECOG 1, weight 70.1 kg, LVEF 45%. Measure LDH and exam at every cycle, track fever, sweats and weight, and record temperatures before any antipyretic. Interim PET-CT after cycle 2 (interpreted with Deauville, 1-3 = favorable); a score of 4-5 triggers tumor board review and a biopsy only if the findings are equivocal, not a reflexive change in therapy. End-of-treatment PET-CT 3-6 weeks after cycle 6, with Deauville 1-3 defining complete metabolic response; a residual Deauville 4-5 with suspicion of progression needs biopsy before any change. Cardiac response monitoring: echocardiogram with GLS before cycle 1 (after 2-3 weeks of GDMT), repeated after cycle 3 and at the end of treatment, and sooner for symptoms or troponin/NT-proBNP rise. After CR, routine imaging is not needed; the breast surveillance mammogram continues annually. Bone marrow re-biopsy only if PET or counts suggest marrow involvement.
answer.pretreatment_workup: 1) Cardio-oncology consult this week. ECG, high-sensitivity troponin and NT-proBNP as baselines. Cardiac MRI with LGE and T1/T2 mapping, or repeat echo with GLS, to separate anthracycline-related from radiation-related or ischemic cardiomyopathy. Coronary evaluation (coronary CT angiography or stress imaging) is reasonable given left-sided chest RT, hypertension and global hypokinesis. 2) Start guideline-directed heart failure therapy now, even though she is asymptomatic (stage B LV dysfunction): ACE inhibitor, ARB or ARNI (preferred for BP and LV function), an evidence-based beta-blocker, and consider an SGLT2 inhibitor per cardio-oncology. Target BP below 130/80. 3) Infection screen given ongoing fever (38.2 C on 2026-09-15): urinalysis, blood cultures if febrile, and chest X-ray given mediastinal disease and prior RT. 4) Labs: repeat CBC with differential, CMP, LDH, uric acid, phosphate, PT/INR, aPTT, quantitative IgG/IgA/IgM (baseline before rituximab), urinalysis, lipid panel and HbA1c if not recent. G6PD only if rasburicase becomes necessary. 5) Hepatitis B: HBsAg, anti-HBc and anti-HBs are nonreactive, so no antiviral prophylaxis is required for rituximab; HBV vaccination is recommended, ideally before cycle 1 (see supportive care). HCV and HIV are negative. 6) Imaging: PET-CT baseline done; brain MRI and LP not routinely indicated (see cns_risk). Ask radiology to add the Deauville score to the baseline PET report. 7) Vascular access: port placement is reasonable for cyclophosphamide and rituximab over 21-day cycles; use the right arm for peripheral IV and BP cuffs because of left axillary surgery, RT and lymphedema risk. 8) Pathology: confirm MYC IHC scoring and whether a second method for MYC rearrangement was used; optional NGS as in biology. 9) Consent discussion with patient and husband covering the anthracycline-free regimen, off-label polatuzumab, expected cure rate, infusion schedule, neuropathy, infection and cardiac monitoring. 10) Pregnancy testing is not needed if postmenopausal (confirm menopausal status).
answer.supportive_care: Heart: GDMT and BP control as above; daily weights at home with a call-in threshold (gain of more than 2 kg in 3 days or new dyspnea or edema); limit IV fluid volume for tumor lysis and infusions. TLS: intermediate risk (bulky disease, elevated LDH, rituximab-chemotherapy). Use allopurinol (or febuxostat) from day -1, with low-volume hydration because of the LV dysfunction; reserve rasburicase for elevated uric acid. Monitor K, phosphate, creatinine. Febrile neutropenia: the regimen is intermediate risk; with age 59, prior chemotherapy and cardiac comorbidity I would give primary G-CSF from cycle 1 (pegfilgrastim or biosimilar, day 2 or later). Penicillin allergy (childhood hives): low risk; cephalosporins such as cefepime are safe for febrile neutropenia; consider penicillin allergy evaluation later. PJP prophylaxis: given 100 mg prednisone for 5 days each cycle for 6 cycles, use atovaquone or TMP-SMX; if TMP-SMX, check potassium closely with ACE inhibitor or ARB and watch counts. Antiviral prophylaxis is not required. Vaccines: inactivated influenza, COVID-19 and pneumococcal now, and HBV vaccine, at least 2 weeks before cycle 1 when feasible; no live vaccines. Antiemetics: NK1 antagonist plus 5-HT3 antagonist, with dexamethasone minimized because prednisone is already in the regimen. Vincristine neuropathy: constipation prevention and neuropathy checks each cycle. Acetaminophen is acceptable at a limited dose; avoid NSAIDs given heart failure risk and renal and platelet concerns. Anastrozole: continue to the planned 10-year endpoint (November 2026) for breast cancer; it has no meaningful interaction with the lymphoma regimen and the lymphoma does not change its indication, but ask the breast team to confirm the stop date given arthralgias and bone loss. Bone health: continue calcium and vitamin D; DEXA is due 2027 but consider moving it earlier because of prednisone and AI exposure. Left arm: lymphedema precautions. Psychosocial and work: social work and oncology nursing, return-to-work planning, and fever-action instructions given to patient and husband.
answer.fitness_and_goals: ECOG 1, NYHA class I, independent in all activities, working full hours, and walking two flights of stairs without stopping; her overall fitness supports curative-intent therapy. The principal constraint is cardiac: LVEF 45% (down from 62%), GLS -14%, mild mitral regurgitation, and uncontrolled BP (148/90), all asymptomatic. Other comorbidities: prior breast cancer on AI, osteopenia, prior anthracycline and chest RT, and a penicillin allergy. She wants cure and to return to full-time work, and is worried about her heart given her mother's heart failure. My recommendation is to tell her plainly that the heart function is the main reason the standard regimen cannot be used, that the plan avoids doxorubicin, that cure is still the goal, that treatment needs a few weeks of heart medicine first, and that the anthracycline-free regimen probably carries a somewhat lower cure rate than standard therapy, which is why trial enrollment is preferred. Answer to her anastrozole question: continue to the planned endpoint and confirm with the breast team. Preserving LV function also matters beyond front-line therapy, because CAR-T or other salvage options at relapse require adequate cardiac function. Realistic return-to-work: likely during treatment with reduced hours, depending on counts and fatigue; plan a reassessment at each cycle.
missing_information: LDH reference range and ULN (the chart flags 510 U/L as high but does not give the ULN; the 2026-03 value of 182 U/L was normal), needed for exact IPI and NCCN-IPI scoring
Deauville score on the baseline PET-CT report and a confirmed PET-CT report of splenic lesions (spleen counted as nodal vs extranodal for staging)
Echocardiogram and GLS values were reported but no repeat LVEF; no cardiac MRI, ECG, troponin or NT-proBNP are in the record; no coronary assessment
Estimated cardiac radiation dose from the 2016 left breast RT plan, and any other chest radiation history
Menopausal status and pregnancy status (assumed postmenopausal; not documented)
Baseline quantitative immunoglobulins (IgG/IgA/IgM), coagulation studies, urinalysis, HbA1c, lipid panel and PT/INR are not in the record
Any second MYC rearrangement method (karyotype or NGS) and whether FISH was performed on a representative tumor block with adequate tumor content
Cell-of-origin by gene expression, MYD88 L265P, CD79B and TP53 status (not performed; would refine prognosis and any trial eligibility)
Infectious or other cause of ongoing fevers (38.2 C on 2026-09-15): no urinalysis, cultures or chest imaging after the PET is in the record
Breast team's decision on the anastrozole stop date (November 2026) and whether to modify endocrine therapy during lymphoma treatment
Medication reconciliation with confirmed doses, including whether any NSAIDs or other agents are in use and whether acetaminophen dosing is documented
Dental, ophthalmic and neurologic baseline status and whether a brain MRI or LP has been done (none documented; not routinely required)
Insurance or drug access for polatuzumab (off-label in this setting) and availability of any open anthracycline-free or cardio-protected lymphoma trials
Patient preferences after the cardiac and efficacy trade-off discussion, including willingness to accept a lower expected cure rate for cardiac safety

items.criterion: The response states the diagnosis is diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (NOS) with a non-germinal-center (non-GCB) phenotype by the Hans algorithm.
The response notes that Hans non-GCB is an immunohistochemical surrogate and is not equivalent to molecular ABC cell-of-origin by gene-expression profiling.
The response states the left axillary node is lymphoma and not recurrent breast carcinoma (cytokeratin AE1/AE3 and GATA3 negative).
The response stages the disease as Lugano/Ann Arbor stage III (nodes on both sides of the diaphragm with splenic involvement).
The response explains that the spleen is lymphatic tissue (a nodal site), so splenic nodules do not make the disease stage IV, and that there is no non-lymphatic extranodal or marrow involvement.
The response notes B symptoms (documented fevers >38 C and drenching night sweats).
The response notes the 7.5 cm mass is below the 10 cm Lugano bulk threshold, acknowledging that bulk definitions vary (some trials use 7.5 cm).
The response stages this patient as stage IV (e.g. by counting splenic involvement as extranodal disease).
The response classifies the lymphoma as double-expressor by IHC (MYC 45% >=40%, BCL2 70% >=50%) but NOT double-hit (FISH shows no MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement).
The response classifies this lymphoma as double-hit / high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements.
The response recommends DA-EPOCH-R (or another intensified regimen) on the basis of double-expressor biology.
The response calculates IPI as 2 (low-intermediate risk): elevated LDH and stage III; age 59, ECOG 1 and no extranodal sites (spleen is not counted as extranodal) score zero.
The response calculates CNS-IPI as 2 (intermediate risk).
The response states that routine CNS prophylaxis is not indicated (CNS-IPI 2, no kidney/adrenal, testicular or breast involvement).
The response mandates CNS prophylaxis (high-dose methotrexate or intrathecal therapy) for this patient.

The response recognizes anthracycline-related cardiac risk (prior doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left chest radiotherapy, LVEF fall from 62% to 45%, i.e. cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction) and does NOT plan standard full-dose doxorubicin (R-CHOP or Pola-R-CHP) without first addressing cardiac function.

The response recommends standard R-CHOP or Pola-R-CHP (full-dose doxorubicin) without conditioning it on the reduced LVEF / prior anthracycline exposure (e.g. without cardio-oncology clearance, a cardioprotective modification, or a non-anthracycline alternative).
The response requests urgent cardio-oncology (or cardiology) evaluation before starting therapy.
The response starts or optimizes guideline-directed cardioprotective therapy: an ACE inhibitor/ARB (or ARNI) plus a beta-blocker (e.g. carvedilol), for example replacing amlodipine.

The response recommends a curative-intent anthracycline-free or anthracycline-modified regimen, e.g. R-CEOP (etoposide in place of doxorubicin) or R-GCVP; R-CHOP with liposomal doxorubicin or dexrazoxane is acceptable only if conditioned on cardio-oncology judging it safe.
The response acknowledges that anthracycline-free regimens likely have lower efficacy than anthracycline-based therapy.
The response plans serial cardiac monitoring during therapy: repeat LVEF/GLS imaging plus troponin and/or natriuretic peptide (BNP/NT-proBNP).
The response recommends palliative-only treatment, best supportive care, or hospice as the plan.
The response plans an end-of-treatment FDG PET-CT read with Lugano criteria / Deauville 5-point scale.
The response assesses tumor lysis risk as low-intermediate (normal creatinine and uric acid, LDH ~2x ULN) and gives allopurinol with hydration for cycle 1.
The response recommends (or reasonably considers) primary G-CSF support with each cycle.
The response addresses the ongoing anastrozole: continuing it is acceptable (no meaningful interaction), or holding it in coordination with breast oncology is also acceptable.
The response confirms hepatitis B serology was checked (HBsAg and anti-HBc nonreactive) before rituximab.
The response judges the patient fit for curative-intent therapy (ECOG 1, normal organ function apart from the LVEF) and acknowledges her goal of cure.
The response lists the cause of the LVEF decline / cardio-oncology work-up as missing (e.g. ischemic evaluation given prior left chest radiotherapy, cardiac MRI, baseline troponin and NT-proBNP).
